id: Textured Paint Art and Wine Night - Three Seashells-The Borough, 162/168 Main Road, Tawa, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Textured Paint Art and Wine Night - Three Seashells
venue: The Borough, 162/168 Main Road, Tawa, Wellington
long_description:
Looking for a creative night out in Wellington? Join us for a fun beginner-friendly adults painting class in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. It’s the perfect excuse to switch off, get creative, and try something a little different.

Whether you’re coming along solo, planning a date night, or organising a catch-up with friends, Paintvine is all about good vibes, creativity, and having fun while you paint – you might even surprise yourself with what you can create!

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

id: Cooking Classes-Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Cooking Classes
venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
For booking a class please contact indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

Just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

long_description:
Ministry of House is back in Session at Superfina!

Saturday December 5th from 9pm - 2am.

Join us for the last time in 2026 as we celebrate Crooked Mind’s birthday.

Banging margaritas from the team at Superfina will be on as per usual!

Ben-Jammin is kicking things off with his signature funky jams, while Crooked Mind will be taking you for a ride with his exclusive UKG takeover set to celebrate another lap around the sun.

Joining Ministry of House for the evening is their friend Joe, better known as PocketLipps.

PocketLipps, a Welly-based selector with over two decades behind the decks, is driven by a lifelong obsession with sound. From his early days in Nelson's river-valley raves to serving up a slew of original edits and productions to peak-time slots at Taniwha’s Denfestival, a sold-out sweat pit at Morning People, & jams with the S-Ence, Breakaway, & High Functioning crews, he’s a master of crafting fluid, unexpected journeys. Expect a seamless blend of funky, gritty, & bumpy house, groovy, jacking techno, lush deep house, & the raw, rhythmic power of UK bass & breaks. Currently delving into production, remixing Welly talent, & crafting his own releases, PocketLipps is a DJ who lives for the shared boogie, always found flailing wildly alongside the crowd.

id: Gallery Orchestra 50th Jubilee and Concert-St James Church, 71 Woburn Road, Lower Hutt-Event Finder
name: Gallery Orchestra 50th Jubilee and Concert
venue: St James Church, 71 Woburn Road, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Celebrate 50 years of music in the Hutt Valley with Gallery Music Centre, Gallery Community Orchestra and friends old and new.

2026 marks 50 years since the founding of the Gallery Orchestra, which later gave rise to the Gallery Music Centre. We are inviting all past students, parents, teaching staff, orchestral conductors and administrators, involved with the orchestra and/or the music centre, to participate in a special concert event to celebrate. Dust off your instrument and join in the rehearsal and performance of massed orchestra items, or just join us for a special shared lunch and concert.

TIME:
10am - 1pm - REHEARSAL for Massed Orchestra/Ensemble items – see more info below
1pm - SHARED LUNCH for anyone with past or present Orchestra or Music Centre involvement
2pm - CONCERT - FREE, ALL WELCOME

MUSIC PARTS: There are parts for a wide variety of playing ability – see the link on the website to view parts to decide which one suits you. You can choose an 'Orchestra' or an 'Ensemble' part. There are 15 short pieces in total. The Pat Sviatko Ensemble will join forces with the orchestra for some of the pieces. Therefore parts marked 'Ensemble' are generally easier than those for the orchestra, and involve playing for up to 7 of the pieces only.
You could also, if desired, come in the weeks leading up to the event, to any number of our regular Saturday morning orchestra/ensemble rehearsals at our weekly rehearsal venue, Dyer Street School, Epuni.
See the website for more information, the music parts, and a form to register your interest in attending any of the parts of the day.

https://gallerymusic.org/jubilee/

You can also help us to assemble our history by sending us any stories, names, information, from past days of the Orchestra or Music Centre.

id: The Great Southern BioBlitz 2026-ZEALANDIA Eco-Sanctuary, Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
name: The Great Southern BioBlitz 2026
venue: ZEALANDIA Eco-Sanctuary, Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington
long_description:
From Friday the 27th to Monday the 30th of November, the tracks of Zealandia will be teeming with citizen scientists (that’s you!) taking part in the Great Southern BioBlitz.

A bioblitz is a great way for communities to get involved in the natural world, learning more about the fauna, flora, and fungi living right under our noses. Spend the weekend taking photos of as many different species as you can to upload to iNaturalist, and watch as experts come along behind you and identify what you have found!

And how can we make that even more exciting? By making a friendly competition out of the event with neighbouring cities by having the most observations recorded! Look out Christchurch!

Anyone can participate and contribute to the wider data base of species in Aotearoa New Zealand. We can’t wait to see your observations from all across the Wellington region, whether that’s here at Zealandia or in your own backyard.

Learn more about the Great Southern BioBlitz.

Image: Lynn Freeman x Fujifilm

id: Talking About Dying, Death and Grief-St Matthew's Anglican Church, 35 Church Street, Masterton-Event Finder
name: Talking About Dying, Death and Grief
venue: St Matthew's Anglican Church, 35 Church Street, Masterton
long_description:
A gentle, practical conversation for the Wairarapa community
Talking openly about serious illness, dying, death and grief can help us feel more prepared, connected and able to support the people we care about.
Join us to explore
• why talking about dying, death and grief matters;
• ways to begin these conversations with family, whānau and friends;
• practical ways to support people who are dying, grieving or caring for someone they love;
• how communities can support one another through serious illness, dying, death and grief.
There will be time for discussion and questions. No prior knowledge or experience is needed.

PRESENTED BY
Dr Ian Gwynne Robson
Medical Director at Te Omanga Hospice, Lower Hutt
Visiting Palliative Specialist in the Wairarapa

Everyone is welcome.
Whatever your experiences, culture, beliefs or relationship with death, this is a respectful space to learn and talk together.
Hosted by Compassionate Communities Wairarapa
For more information or to RSVP: Bernie at Compassionate Communities
compassionatewairarapa@gmail.com

id: Tū Rangatahi-Te Rauparaha Arena, 17 Parumoana St, Porirua - Mana-Event Finder
name: Tū Rangatahi
venue: Te Rauparaha Arena, 17 Parumoana St, Porirua - Mana
long_description:
Tū Rangatahi is a free suicide prevention day for rangatahi, run by Te Waka Whaiora at Te Rauparaha Arena in Porirua.

It’s run for rangatahi and led by rangatahi. The day is about looking out for your mates, your loved ones and yourself, and knowing where to go if you or someone close to you needs help.

The speakers are people who started at the bottom and got somewhere. Between the talks there are rap battles, singing and a school choir. The MCs are Porirua community leader Daniel Filemoni and his nephew, comedian Laban Miller.

Local services will have stalls on the day, and Te Waka Whaiora’s rangatahi team will run a quiet space for anyone who needs a break.

There’s a free sausage sizzle and prize draws. It’s open to all ages, so bring the whānau, and you don’t need to register.

Schools and groups can contact Tyla at tyla@tww.org.nz.

If this raises anything for you, free help is available any time. Call or text 1737, or call Lifeline on 0800 543 354 or Youthline on 0800 376 633 (free text 234).

id: Night Shift: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future-City Gallery Wellington, Civic Square, 101 Wakefield St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Night Shift: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
venue: City Gallery Wellington, Civic Square, 101 Wakefield St, Wellington
long_description:
Night Shift brings short talks, exhibition tours, and hands-on activities inspired by the world of Cornelia Parker to three Thursday evenings.

Come with friends or on your own, explore at your own pace, and linger over a drink at āta.

Join two Aotearoa writers whose fiction ventures into the unknown: Pip Adam, winner of the 2026 Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction, and Terri Te Tau, author of The Valley of Unlikely Acquaintances and member of the artist collective Mataaho.

With titles like The Future (Sixes & Sevens) and Through a Glass Darkly, Cornelia Parker’s artworks swirl with the sense that nothing is quite settled. Crawl inside that feeling with us.

--

Programme

5.30pm & 7.30pm: Exhibition Tours
Take a closer look at Cornelia Parker on a 45-minute guided tour. First come, first served.

5.30pm, 6.15pm, 7pm, 7.45pm: Step Inside the Darkroom
The Handmade Darkroom Collective is taking over our classroom and turning it into a working photographic darkroom. Inspired by Cornelia Parker, you are invited to make your own A5-sized photogram, playing with directional light and objects of significance or visual interest. Feel free to bring along some small trinkets you may wish to print with. 

Each time slot has a 16-person capacity, on a first-in-first-served basis. Please queue at the classroom door (upstairs) before the session you wish to attend. 

6.15pm & 6.45pm: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
Two short talks with writers Pip Adam and Terri Te Tau, inspired by Cornelia Parker.

7.00–8.00pm: Behind the Scenes: Cornelia Parker
How do you hang an explosion? Meet some of the people who installed the exhibition and care for its artworks. Drop in, ask questions and find out what it takes to bring this exhibition to life.

--

Tickets Required
2-for-1 Tickets
Adult $25
Concession $22

id: Wetland Explore Experience-Green Jersey Explorer Tours, 16 Kitchener Street, Martinborough, Martinborough-Event Finder
name: Wetland Explore Experience
venue: Green Jersey Explorer Tours, 16 Kitchener Street, Martinborough, Martinborough
long_description:
Born from the shared vision of the Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation, Green Jersey Cycle Tours, Hau Ariki Marae, and the Aorangi Restoration Trust, this experience offers a meaningful way to connect and contribute to the natural world. We weave conservation, culture, arts and science into an immersive journey.

You will go off the beaten track and step into little known pockets of wildlife, meeting the people who are actively restoring them. At Ruamāhanga Farm, you will get hands-on with the restoration work yourself. At the lake along with the sounds of the night you will hear stories and original songs born directly from this landscape through our Te Reo o te Wai project. Beside the awa and in the heart of the bush, there will be guided space to slow down, reflect, and explore your own creativity.

id: Experience HU: A Spiritual Sound Meditation-Ōtaki Memorial Hall, Main St, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Experience HU: A Spiritual Sound Meditation
venue: Ōtaki Memorial Hall, Main St, Ōtaki
long_description:
Explore a daily spiritual practice for more joy, wisdom, peace

HU is an active meditation mantra that can help quiet the mind, open the heart, and awaken a deeper sense of love, wisdom, and inner awareness.

HU (pronounced like hue) is known as the sound behind all sounds—a carrier of divine love between the Creator and you. It’s not limited to any religion or belief system and can enhance any path you’re already on.

You are welcome to join us to sing HU and discover what this sacred sound may awaken within you.

What to expect:
• We will begin with a short inspirational reading
• then sing HU for 15-20 minutes
• followed by a few minutes of quiet contemplative time
• you are welcome to stay for relaxed spiritual conversation and refreshments afterwards.

No previous experience is needed. Everyone is welcome to join, listen, and take part in whatever way feels comfortable.

This is a free event

Want to experience HU before joining us? - Listen to the HU song or download the free HU app at www.hearhu.org (see live link above)

Venue: Otaki Memorial Hall supper room, 9 Aotaki Street

Feel free to register or just drop in. We would love to see you!

For more information please contact Lorraine 021464325.

An entertaining guide to the universe’s deadliest environments.

The remarkable robots and machines exploring space on humanity’s behalf.

name: Public Lecture: The Role of Religion in 21st Century Public Life
venue: St John's in the City Presbyterian Church, 170 Willis Street., Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
This free public lecture 'The Role of Religion in 21st Century Public Life: Finding a Consistent Ethic in an Age of Christian Nationalism' explores the nature of the interaction between faith and politics.

Professor Millies is an eminent Christian scholar, author, lecturer and political science theorist whose work explores this question in a time of significant political volatility as well as conflicting understandings of Christianity’s role in ordering our public life.

Wednesday 2nd December – 7.00pm

WHO: Professor Steven Millies – Professor of Public Theology, Catholic Theological Union, Chicago
WHERE: St John’s in the City – corner Dixon & Willis St.

A collaboration between St John’s in the City and Te Kupenga – the NZ Catholic Leadership Institute.
